lawyer:
Dr M Zahir with Subrata Chowdhury, Advocates -----For the Petitioner. 
Mahmudul Hoque, Advocate -----For the Respondent Nos. 2-4.
parties:
Chittagong Container Transportation Company -----Petitioner 
Vs. 
Government of Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Raisuddin, J : On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, the petitioner obtained the Rule calling upon the respondent to show cause as to why a direction should not be issued upon the respondents for fixing and realisation of open space rent from the petitioner in respect of container yard measuring 51 526 square metre yard outside the Chittagong port protected area at half of the rate of the rent of covered space as envisaged in Regulation 163(2) of the Regulation for Working of Chittagong Port (Cargo and Container), 2001 read with Tariff Item Nos. 212 and 273 and with note-I relating to space rent of the schedule of cargo and goods and vessels, etc. instead of rate of rent as mentioned in the order or renewal under memo No. DT/SR/OAS/2003-02 dated 6-3-2005 signed and issued by the Director (Traffic), Chittagong Port Authority, respondent No.3 contained in Annexure-H and as to why the order under memo No.নৌপম/চবশা/১আ-১/৯৬ (অংশ-২) ১২৫ dated 17-2- 2005 signed and issued by the respondent No. 1 for charging open space rent in outside the port protected area contained in Annexure-G should not be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. Relevant facts for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the petitioner filed an application on 20-10-2003 before the Chittagong Port Authority (hereinafter referred as CPA), respondent No.2 for leasing out land measuring 50,000 square metre open space outside port protected area at X and Y shed compound of the CPA on open space rent. The CPA Board gave decision in favour of the petitioner for leasing out 51526 square metre initially for one year on payment of space rent as per Tariff Item No. 27 of the Schedule of Charges regulated by Regulation 163(2) of the Regulations for Working of Chittagong Port (Cargo and Container), 2001. Upon decision given by the CPA Board, agreement for leasing out of 51526 square metre open space outside the port protected area was concluded in the prescribed form under Rule 163 of the General Rules and Schedules for working of Chittagong Port covered storage for a period of 1(one) year from 1-12-2003 to 30-11-2004 @ Taka 20+15% VAT per square metre per month signed on 15-12-2003. On physical survey and measurement of the land by 3 member committee constituted by the CPA handed over the petitioner the open space measuring 48493.35 square metres vide memo dated 1-1-2004 and subsequently on the application of the petitioner dated 14-2-2004 and upon the recommendation of the CPA under memo dated 24-2-1004 the Ministry of Shipping issued no objection certificate under memo dated 26-i-2004 for construction of a container yard and container freight station. The petitioner availing the facilities built a container yard by investing over Taka 100 million. As per agreement dated 15-12-2003, the petitioner started payment of rent in a letter dated 15-12-2003 at the rate of Taka 10 per square metre per month and paid first installment of Taka 70,196 vide pay order dated 15-12-2003 for the period of December, 2003 and January, 2004 with a request for adjustment in his account by calculating half rate of rent for the covered space. The CPA raised objection to the payment of open space rent Taka 10 per square metre per month as stated above and directed the petitioner to make payment at the rate of Taka 20 per metre per month as per Tariff item 2.7.2 of the Schedule of charge on goods and vessels vide memo dated 11-8-2004. The petitioner challenged the above decision dated 11-8- 2004 with demand for realisation of open space rent, @ Taka 10 per square metre per month highlighting the previous record of realisation of the open space rent at Taka 10 from the Government undertaking, namely Trading Corporation of Bangladesh and present realisation from Bay Fishing Limited a private concern. Upon the letter of Ministry of Shipping dated 18-10-2004 the respondent No. 4 admitting the realisation of open space at the rate of Taka 10 per square metre from the Trading Corporation of Bangladesh and Messrs Bay Fishing gave a reply under memo dated 1-12-2004 interpreting the relevant Regulations 163(1), 163(2) of the Regulations for Working of Chittagong Port (Cargo and Container), 2001 covering Note No. 1 relating to Tariff item 2.7 on space rent and remaining in its old stand and thereby insisted realisation of open space rent from the petitioner at the rate of Taka 20. After approach by the petitioner vide letter dated 14-9- 2004 and respondent No.2 under memo dated 1-12- 2004, the respondent No. 1 took opinion of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. The respondent No.3 quoting the said approach of the petitioner in letters dated 14-9-2004 and 17-2-2005 of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs gave decision directing the petitioner under memo dated 6-3-2005 on a self/made interpretation of the Regulation 163(1) and 163(2) of the Regulations for Working of Chittagong Port (Cargo and Container), 2001 and note-1 of the said Tariff item renewal of Agreement for one year on payment of rent at the rate of lease agreement with all payable dues. After receiving the said memo, the petitioner served Demand of Justice Notice upon the respondents on 10-3-2005 for dispensing justice to it but received no reply. Hence the Rule. 

 3. The respondent Nos. 2-4 contested the Rule by filing Affidavit-in-opposition denying the material averments made in the writ petition contending, inter alia, that on an application of the petitioner dated 20-10-2003 and recommendation of the Minister for Ministry of Shipping, the CPA Board i.e. the, respondent No. 4 vide its decision dated 17-11-2004 decided to lease put 51526 square metre space for one year on payment of space rent as per Tariff item No. 2.7.2 of the schedule of charges and Regulation 163(2) of the Regulations' for Working of Chittagong Port (Cargo, and Container), 2001. Accordingly, an agreement under Rule 163 for letting out 51526 square metre space outside the port protected area was concluded in the prescribed form for the period 1-12-2004 @ Taka 20 + 15% VAT per square metre as agreed by the petitioner. Upon agreement between the parties, the petitioner started payment of rent at the rate agreed upon in the agreement and the petitioner paid monthly rent up to September 2004. While the petitioner making payment of the rent it unilaterally raised a demand that they are entitled to pay rent at half of the rate. The respondents vide their letters dated 4-14-2004, 10-5-2004, 6-6-2004, 11-7-2004, 8-8-2004 and 16-8-2004 replied to the petitioner denying their claim of paying rent at half of the rate and demanded payment of arrear rents at the rate as per the said agreement and Regulation 163(2) of the Regulations, for Working of Chittagong Port (Cargo and Container), 2001 and Tariff item No. 2.7.2 of Schedule of Charges. The petitioner on 14-9-2004 made a representation to the Secretary, Ministry of Shipping for realisation of rent VAT the rate of Taka 10 per square metre from the petitioner. The Ministry of Shipping referred the matter to the respondent No. 2 asking him to reply about some queries vide letter dated, 18- 10-2004. The respondents vide their letter dated 1-12-2004 replied to the quarries made by the Ministry of Shipping and in that reply the factual position and law has been explained. The Ministry of Shipping on receiving the reply to the queries referred the matter to the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs for further opinion. The Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs has opined vide memo dated 6-2-2005 that the rate of rent was agreed by the petitioner and the tenure of the agreement has already been expired and, as such, there having no scope for addition, alteration and revision in the agreement, the claim of the petitioner is not sustainable both in fact as well as in law. The respondent No. 1 upon receipt of the opinion from the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs communicated the same to the petitioner. The respondent No. 2 vide letter dated 17-2-2005 requested to take necessary steps in this regard. The respondent No.3 vide letter dated 6-3- 2005 (Annexure-H) communicated the opinion of the Ministry of Shipping to the petitioner explaining the actual situation and position of law in this regard and requested the petitioner to pay up to date rent for the space let out to them at the rate as agreed upon in the agreement and to have the agreement renewed for further one year on the same terms and conditions and in the alternative if they are not at all willing to renew the agreement, to surrender the space to the respondent by giving 14 days notice as per c1ause-2 of the agreement dated 15-12-2003. It has been further stated that the petitioner has challenged the memo dated 17-2-2005 (Annexure- G) given by the respondent No. 1 communicating the opinion of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs which is merely an opinion of the Law Ministry. By that letter no action was taken against the petitioner. By the memo dated 6-3-2005 (Annexure-H) the respondent No.3 communicated the letter and opinion contained in Shipping Ministry's letter dated 17-2-2005 to the petitioner. Those memos , are issued on the basis of the petitioner's letter dated 14-9-2004 and by the said memo nothing new has been imposed upon the petitioner by the respondents. Therefore the petitioner has got no locus standi to challenge the legality of the said memos issued by the respondents. The respondents issued the said letters asking the petitioner to adjust up to date rent and to renew the agreement for further period of 1(one) year on the same terms and conditions or surrender the space to the respondents. 

 4. The petitioner filed supplementary affidavit showing that the open space rented out to the petitioner was originally marshy land which has been improved and developed by the petitioner at his own expense incurring over Taka 10 crore with prior approval of the respondents for accommodating the loaded and unloaded containers and in support the petitioner annexed some photographs. 

 6. Dr M Zahir appearing with Mr Subrata Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the petitioner has not challenged the agreement which has already expired on 30-11-2004 but the petitioner has challenged the order of renewal vide memo dated 6-3-2005 (Annexure-H) issued by the CPA and refusal of payment at the rate of Taka 10 per square metre per month in place of Taka 20 per square metre per month for the covered space as opined by the respondent No. 1 on the ground of expiry of the lease agreement (Annexure- G). The learned Advocate further submits that interpretation and opinion are not applicable since the petitioner's case relates to Regulation 163(2) of the General Rules and Schedule of Charges. He next submits that the management of the port and tariff is regulated by the provisions of Regulation for Working of Chittagong Port (Cargo and Container), 2001 enacted as per section 19 of the Chittagong Port Authority Ordinance, 1976 wherein Regulation 163 relating to space rent. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the application of the petitioner dated 20-10-2003 agreement and delivery of possession shows that the petitioner rented area open space covered under Regulation 163(2) and schedule of charges provided in tariff item No. 2.7.2 read with note-I shall be applicable in case of the petitioner and, as such, the Rule should be made absolute. 

 7. Mr Mahmudul Hoque, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 2-4 at the very outset submits that this writ petition is not maintainable since the petitioner filed the writ petition after expiry of lease agreement as well as the petitioner is a defaulter in payment of rent. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate relied upon the decision in the case of Chaila Khal Nobam Khanda Mathshy Samababy Samity Ltd vs Revenue Deputy Collector and Ex Officio Member Secretary and others, reported in 1 BLC 339 and in the case of Mallikpur Fishermen Co-operative Society Limited vs Secretary, Ministry of Land and others, reported in 1995 BLD (AD) 241. Mr Hoque next submits that the lease agreement executed between the parties is not a statutory contract rather the same is an ordinary lease. Therefore, the petitioner cannot invoke the writ jurisdiction to enforce any right arising out of the lease agreement. In support of his contention, he relied in the case of Ananda Builders Ltd vs Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority, reported in 57 DLR (AD) 31 and in the case of Bangladesh Power Development Board vs Md Asad-uz-zaman Sikder, reported in 9 BLC (AD) 1. 

 9. Fourthly, he submits that the lease was given to the petitioner under Rules 163(2) of Regulations for Working of Chittagong Port, 2001 and under Tariff Item No. 2.7.2 of the Schedule of the charge which clearly shows that space rent outside the Port protected area shall be Taka 20 per square metre per month. 

 10. Mr Hoque lastly submits that issuance of notice dated 6-3-2005 (Annexure-H) asking the lessee petitioner to pay arrear rents and to have the lease renewed at the rate proposed and agreed in the agreement or in alternative to vacate the premises by giving 14 days notice under Clause-Z of the agreement which is in accordance with law, as such the Rule should be discharged. 

 12. On perusal of the record, it appears that admittedly there was an agreement in between the parties under Rule 163 of the General Rules and Schedule for Working of the Chittagong Port Covered Storage of Goods in Chittagong Port Authority. The agreement was made for a period of one year with effect from 1-12-2003 to 30-11-2004 at the rate of Taka 20 + 15% VAT per square metre. The petitioner accordingly paid the rents up to January of 2004. All on a sudden the petitioner raised the claim that the space rented to the petitioner by the Chittagong Port Authority shall be at the rate of Taka 10 per square metre per month. The claim raised by the petitioner was sent to the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs for legal opinion and after obtaining the legal opinion, the respondent No.4, Chittagong Port Authority issued the notice on 6-3- 2005 to the petitioner to pay the arrear rent and after payment of arrear rent either to renew the lease at the rate proposed and agreed or in alternative to vacate the premises as per clause 2 of the agreement between the parties. The petitioner challenged that memo and also sought for direction by this Court to pay the rent at the rate of Taka 10 per square metre per month. 

 14. In order to appreciate the argument of the parties schedule of charges the relevant Tariff item NG. 2.7 is quoted as under: 2.7 Space Rent. (Authority as against tariff item No. 22 above) 

 2.7.1 Space rent inside port protected area for cargo: 

 2.7.2 Space rent outside area for Cargo.	do	Tk. 20 

 2.7.3 Space rent inside and outside	do	Tk. 20 

 2.7.4 Space rent international Transit	do	Tk.40 

 Cargo-see note (vi) Notes: (i) Open areas will be charged space rent at half rate. (ii) Time is counted after the issue of storage order by CPA. The day on which the storage order issued is not counted for space rent. (iii) For the period before space rent is charged, the cargo will be charged wharf rent, according to tariff item 2.6. (iv) Movement of cargo between (1) the place of wharf rent (2) the place of space rent is the responsibility of the shipper/ consignee. (v) Space rent is only provided for an area of 100 square metres or more, per consignment. (vi) For the purpose of this tariff item. International Transit Cargo is defined as cargo under Special Arrangement, which will pass through Bangladesh before delivery in another country. This definition excludes transshipment reshipment cargo. 

 15. The agreement has been signed in between the parties as per Regulation 163, of Regulations for Working of Chittagong Port (cargo and container), 2001. Regulation 163 contains two parts. Firstly, 163(1) deals with the space which is available in storage sheds inside Port protected area and that Regulations contains xiv Sub-Regulations wherein Sub-Regulation xii categorically says that open areas will be charged at half of the Tariff rate. Secondly, Regulation 163(2) deals with space rent outside port protected area and it does not have any Sub-Regulation like that of Regulation 163(1). So the contention of the petitioner that open will be charged at half of the Tariff rate is not contended in this Sub-Regulation. In the present case, the space let out is outside the port protected area and it falls within the Regulation 163(2) which admittedly does not contain any Sub-Regulation as to the rate. The contention of the petitioner that the schedule of charges, contains in note under 2.7 wherein note (i) says that rent of the open areas will be half The Regulations and the charge of schedule are read together and accordingly the levy is to be calculated. If we read both this together then it appears that Regulation 163(2) does not have any Sub-Regulations which would attract that the rent of open space shall be half of the rate. So the note contained in charge of schedule does not have any nexus with Regulation 163(2), the note shall be in Regulation 163(1) as the Sub-Regulation indicates the same. 

 18. For the reasons and discussions made hereinabove, we do not find any illegality in the impugned order asking the petitioner to adjust the up to date rent for the space let out to them at the rate agreed upon and mentioned in the agreement and to have the agreement renewed for further 1(one) year on the same terms and conditions and/or in the alternative, surrender the space to the respondents by giving 14 days' notice as per clause 2 of the agreement. Therefore, we find no merit in this Rule:
